negative_reviews.author: E R
negative_reviews.text:
The ramen was quite delightful, however there is one major concern. The hygiene/cleanliness of the glassses.

The glasses we received had varying cleanliness, the first glass ( the solo one shown in the image) was quite dirty. It had grime left on it, at first we thought it was because of the ice however it did not go away. It is just dissapointing considering that the food was excellent and the atmosphere is perfect.

The 2nd glass was considerably cleaner ( shown in the image with the other glass next to it). I am sure they will be able to improve this

issues: Three negative reviews covered front of house service speed and attentiveness, and a heater needing replacement.
Reviews also raised badly scratched glassware, which has been thrown away with a replacement order placed.
A new cooking pot was bought, and the standard is now a maximum of two packs of chicken broth per cook rather than three.
Staff must taste test each new batch of broth before serving and avoid over preparing broth late at night, as it darkens overnight.
Stock cover was sufficient with no shortages in the week.
Weekday trade was very quiet with little town centre footfall while the weekend was busier than usual, and labour was cut back as far as possible.
New chairs and tables are outstanding with no stock available, so the site has asked whether it can buy ad hoc or borrow from another site.
Collection of recyclable items from the back of the restaurant has been requested.
A new freezer is outstanding and queued behind the Glasgow installation.
One team member continues to work three to four days a week here as their primary role, picking up extra hours elsewhere to meet their required hours.
Site level food cost figures remain a week behind pending head office data.

Region-wide (England): The prep level list in the daily Mapal chef report is being replaced by a nightly main protein stock count, recorded on a printed sheet in the kitchen and photographed and uploaded to Mapal every night by whoever closes.

Region-wide (England): The AI daily stock ordering dashboard is only as accurate as the daily stock counts and timely invoice entry into Kobas, and two sites this week showed false shortage flags caused by invoice upload lag.
Region-wide (England): Operations is sourcing a new Char Siu and karaage manufacturer after supplier size inconsistency drove wastage and food cost.
actions: Taste test each new batch of chicken broth before service and hold to two packs per cook - Owner: Jason (15/09/2026)
Confirm whether chairs and tables can be bought ad hoc or borrowed from another site - Owner: Francheska (15/09/2026)
Arrange collection of the recyclable items from the back of the restaurant - Owner: Francheska (15/09/2026)
Sort the new freezer for the site once the Glasgow installation is complete - Owner: Ross Ward (15/09/2026)
Region-wide (England): Print and laminate the new stock tracking sheet and post it visibly in the kitchen - Owner: All sites (15/09/2026)
Region-wide (England): Count main protein and prep stock on every closing shift and upload the photographed sheets to Mapal nightly - Owner: All sites (15/09/2026)
